questions.q: Which earlier chapter's checkpointing discipline is the reason Lesson 31's incident wasted compute rather than lost training progress?
options: Chapter 6, Cost Optimization
Chapter 3, Distributed Training Infrastructure
Chapter 4, Model Serving and Inference Infrastructure
Chapter 1, GPU Computing Fundamentals
questions.explain: Chapter 3's checkpointing and fault-tolerance material is why the training job had already saved its final checkpoint successfully before the stall -- the incident cost money, not training progress.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what distinction does Chapter 5's MLOps material draw that matters for understanding Lesson 31's gap?
options: Infrastructure-level alerting (job duration, GPU utilization) is a different kind of monitoring than model-quality monitoring like drift detection -- Lesson 31's gap was the former, not the latter
Chapter 5 has nothing to do with monitoring of any kind
Model-quality monitoring and infrastructure alerting are identical and interchangeable
Chapter 5 only covers CI/CD and never discusses monitoring
questions.explain: Lesson 31's incident was a gap in infrastructure-level alerting, distinct from the model-quality drift monitoring Chapter 5 covers -- a distinction worth keeping clear.

questions.q: What Chapter 7 idea does Lesson 30's decision to skip a PodDisruptionBudget on the scale-to-zero endpoint actually reflect?
options: That PodDisruptionBudgets are deprecated and should never be used
That scale-to-zero endpoints should always have a PDB regardless of cost
The SLO framework's deliberate availability-versus-cost tradeoff -- choosing not to always default to 'protect availability' without weighing what it costs
That Chapter 7 is unrelated to any decision made in this capstone
questions.explain: Lesson 27's SLO framework is exactly about making availability-versus-cost tradeoffs on purpose, which is what skipping the PDB here represents.

questions.q: How many Expert Specialization courses does this course belong to in the Cloud Engineer -> Cloud Architect path, and in what order must they be taken?
options: Two courses, taken together simultaneously
Four courses, which build on the Advanced Specialization stage but not on each other, so they can be taken in any order
Four courses, which must be taken in a strict fixed sequence starting with this one
Six courses, each requiring all the others to be completed first
questions.explain: This course is one of four Expert Specialization courses (alongside Advanced Platform Engineering/GitOps/CI-CD, Hybrid & Multi-Cloud Enterprise Architecture, and Advanced SRE/Disaster Recovery/Resilience) that build on the Advanced stage but not on each other, so there's no fixed order among them.

questions.q: What does this lesson say was actually proved across this capstone's three lessons?
options: That each lesson taught a brand-new skill never covered earlier in the course
That GPU infrastructure requires no cost monitoring at all
That this course's seven earlier chapters, used together on one continuous storyline, are enough to provision a real cluster, deploy a real endpoint, and understand a real class of cost incident
That distributed training and model serving are unrelated topics with no shared infrastructure
questions.explain: None of the three capstone lessons introduced a new skill -- each one combined earlier chapters together on one continuous storyline instead of testing them in isolation.
